assumptions: The control file must sit directly in the delivery folder; a file named CONTROL_x.txt in a sub-folder counts as an ordinary file.
A file at the package root outside any delivery folder makes the package be refused.
If two files in one delivery folder share a name (e.g. in different sub-folders), the move fails on the name clash rather than overwriting.
The manifest does not list itself; it covers only the files under data/.
The count n excludes the control file itself and includes files in sub-folders.

steps.pseudocode:
1. files = pkg.files(); if empty, pkg.fail('empty package').
2. Group files by first path segment. A file at the package root (no '/') -> pkg.fail('file outside a delivery folder').
3. For each delivery folder: controls = files directly in the folder (path == folder/name, no deeper '/') whose name fully matches CONTROL_(\d+)\.txt.
4. If len(controls) == 0 -> pkg.fail('no control file in <folder>'); if len(controls) > 1 -> pkg.fail('more than one control file in <folder>').
5. others = number of files in the folder (sub-folders included) minus the one control file.
6. If int(n) != others -> pkg.fail('control count mismatch in <folder>').
7. Do not change any files.
steps.title: Verify each delivery folder has one control file with a matching file count
Move files to data/<delivery folder>/<file name>, dropping sub-folders
Compute md5 and sha256 for every file
Write manifest.csv with path, size, md5 and sha256

output.summary: Checks that every top-level delivery folder has exactly one CONTROL_<n>.txt whose n equals the number of other files in that folder, and refuses the whole package otherwise. It then removes the control files and moves all remaining files to data/<delivery folder>/<file name>, dropping sub-folders. Finally it computes md5 and sha256 for each file and writes manifest.csv at the root.
